To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inclusion of hemp products in the diet of laying hens does not adversely affect their performance and leads to an enrichment of the n3 fatty acid content in eggs.

feeding hemp seed or hemp seed oil to laying hens up until 20 and 10%, respectively, does neither adversely affect the performance of laying hen, nor does it affect egg quality, but leads to the enrichment in the n-3 content of eggs.
feeding HS and HO diets to laying hens does not adversely affect hen performance and leads to an enrichment of the n3-fatty acid content of eggs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of hemp as a novel source for the enrichment of eggs with n-3 fatty acids.
the effects of feeding hemp seed (HS, 20% in the diet) or hemp seed (HO, 4, 6, or 8% in the diet, respectively) on laying hen performance, egg quality, and fatty acid profile of egg yolk.
the effect of dietary hemp seed and hemp oil on laying hen production and the fatty acid composition of eggs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of hemp products as feed additives is safe for laying hens and can be recommended for egg yolk enrichment with n-3 fatty acids.
hemp products can be used in laying hen diets to enrich eggs with n-3 fatty acids without affecting performance.
HS and HO can be used safely and efficiently in laying hen diets to increase the n-3 content of eggs.

hemp seed is a good source of protein and fiber and can be included up to a maximum of 20% in the diets of egg-laying hens.
hemp seed and hemp oil are safe and efficient feed ingredients for laying hen diets, which can be used to produce n-3 enriched eggs.
hemp seed is an excellent feed ingredient for laying hen diets, and it is safe to use in diets at levels as high as 20%.
